MAJOR: `main.go` degradation startup guard: only refuses when `PF_EDP_DEGRADATION_CONFIG` is set; an invalid/malformed default `config/edp-degradation.json` still falls back to an empty policy, silently disabling AC-4 fail-closed `CONFIG_INVALID` behavior.

`degrade/policy.go`: hardcoded `p.renewals[store] > 3` makes `Check` return `ErrDegradedExpired` for every operation once a store has accumulated renewals, with no reset/alert in the hunk; healthy or removed rules cannot recover without process restart.

`bench/harness.go` + `bench/slo.go`: `Measure` breaks on the first error, so `Errors` is effectively 0/1; any `max_errors >= 2` can never be exceeded, silently disabling the error SLO bound the delta intends to enforce.

`cache/memory.go`: eviction triggers on `len >= 10000` by deleting a random live entry, including when `Set` is only updating an existing key; capacity is hardcoded and untracked by an eviction metric, so one tenant's writes can churn/evict other tenants without visibility.
MINOR: `cache/memory.go` / `main.go`: tenant namespacing is implemented only at the handler (`tenant + ":" + key`); the cache store API remains tenant-unaware, so any future direct caller can bypass isolation.
`db_explain_capture.py`: a sampled-in request refused by `rate_ok` is returned without an audit record, so the audit log does not capture the sample/refusal decision.
`main.go` object conform now requires `tenant`; no delta update to callers/runbook, so existing operator scripts invoking the admin endpoint without `tenant` will break.
NIT: `cache/memory.go`: random map-range eviction is non-deterministic and ignores TTL/expiry, which can make cache/bench behavior less repeatable.
`db_explain_capture.py`: the new state/audit requirement applies only when `sample_rate > 0`; the skip path still calls `audit(None)` if audit is absent.
SUMMARY: Delta resolves the prior build/unused-local and handler tenant-prefix issues, but several fixes are incomplete at the boundaries.

Top risks: default degradation config can still be silently swallowed; renewal cap can permanently fail-closed without recovery; benchmark error counts cannot enforce `max_errors>1`; cache eviction can cause cross-tenant churn without metrics.
